anomaly_def.Name: Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly + Database Memory Allocation Anomaly + Transaction Log Subsystem Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly: Concurrent transactions request incompatible locks on the same resource, creating blocking chains or deadlocks that stall forward progress.
Database Memory Allocation Anomaly: Aggregate memory consumed by caches, work areas, and session heaps surpasses the safe capacity of the host, provoking paging or out-of-memory pressure.
Transaction Log Subsystem Anomaly: Commit processing is throttled because log buffers, log files, or archiving pipelines cannot absorb the volume of redo being generated.

When these three root causes strike together, the database exhibits an intertwined symptom set: lock-wait time and deadlock frequency rise while commit latency simultaneously elongates; worker threads pile up in both lock-manager wait queues and OS run queues starved for memory; RSS and swap usage climb until the operating system steals cache pages, further degrading buffer-cache hit ratios; log-flush and log-write waits spike, exaggerating the apparent duration of locks held during COMMIT; connection pools saturate, application timeouts increase, and recovery/instance restarts may occur when memory exhaustion or stalled log archival triggers fault-management logic.

Causally, each anomaly amplifies the others. Memory pressure slows SQL execution (extra paging, reduced cache efficiency), lengthening transaction lifetimes and thereby prolonging lock holds that intensify contention. The enlarged lock backlog inflates per-session memory footprints (lock structures, row versions, private work areas), deepening the memory shortfall. Prolonged transactions also generate more redo per unit of business work and keep old log segments active, causing log files to fill faster; in turn, delayed log flushes extend commit duration so locks remain held even longer, feeding the contention loop. Finally, frequent flushes and checkpoint storms consume additional CPU and memory buffer space, tightening the memory bottleneck and creating a self-reinforcing triad that can bring an OLTP system to a near standstill if not addressed holistically.

entry.official_definition: Aborts any statement that waits longer than the specified amount of time while attempting to acquire a lock.
entry.trigger_condition: A statement waits longer than lock_timeout for a table, index, row, or other database object lock.
entry.workload_impact: The statement attempting to acquire the lock is aborted.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when a statement cannot obtain the required lock within the configured waiting window because another transaction or metadata operation is holding an incompatible lock.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect blocking sessions, reduce conflicting transaction overlap, shorten transaction lifetime, and review lock scheduling and schema-change timing.
